sentences.text: The only valid species, Nanantius eos, was first described in 1986.
Nanantius eos has been classified as an enantiornithean, a group of primitive Cretaceous birds that did not survive the mass extinction.
It is classified within the family Alexornithidae.
Evidence of Nanantius being seabirds includes a tibiotarsus found in the gut of an ichthyosaur specimen QM F16811.
The holotype specimen was found at Warra Station near Boulia in Queensland.
In 1997, additional fossils from Canary Station in Australia were assigned to the genus Nanantius.
A partial left tibiotarsus was assigned to Nanantius but excluded from N. eos due to anatomical differences.
A supposed second species, Nanantius valifanovi, was found to be a synonym of Gobipteryx minuta.
Nanantius is tentatively placed in a clade closely related to Vorona, Grabauornis, and Yungavolucris.
Nanantius inhabited the Eromanga Sea and its surroundings, a large inland sea in what is now Australia, during the Early Cretaceous.
The fossil record of Nanantius spans from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Nanantius belongs to Enantiornithes because its tibiotarsus characters are not sufficiently diagnostic.
